clue.text: Give prisoner commendation

parts.note: con is slang for a convict
a tribute is an expression of praise

explanation.surface: An inmate is handed some praise, perhaps for good behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: To contribute is to donate or hand over, as when giving to a charity.

clue.text: Better to catch river fish

indicators.note: catching something means holding it, so the word for better encloses the letter

parts.note: to cap something is to better it

explanation.surface: An angler hopes to land a better catch than a mere river fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The carp is a freshwater fish.

clue.text: Weep with sprain, upset and losing one's rag

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disturbed, so the letters are rearranged
losing means doing without, so one letter is dropped from the word sprain

parts.note: I looks like the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone cries over a sprained ankle and loses their temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing one's' takes I out of SPRAIN; 'upset' rearranges WEEP plus SPRAN. 'Losing one's rag' is British for losing one's temper.
explanation.definitionFit: Rag is a dismissive slang term for a newspaper, especially a poor one.

clue.text: Rebel pinches new hair colouring

indicators.note: pinching means gripping between, so the word for rebel holds the letter

parts.note: to rise up is to rebel

explanation.surface: A rebel steals a new hair dye.
explanation.definitionFit: A rinse is a temporary tint washed into the hair.

clue.text: Jumped on wild pig and went belly up? Not I!

parts.note: a boar is a wild pig

indicators.note: Not I says the letter I is to be left out of the word before

parts.note: to go belly up is to die, as a dead fish floats

explanation.surface: A wild pig was ridden and then died, though the speaker survived.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not I' drops the I from DIED to leave DED.
explanation.definitionFit: To board a vehicle is to get on it, so boarded means jumped on.

clue.text: Aerial warning storm's coming?

parts.note: aerial here means in the air or sky: a rumble from the sky warns of an approaching storm

explanation.surface: A broadcast mast picks up a warning that a storm is on its way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Aerial' suggests a TV antenna, but here it means something heard from the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Rumbling from the sky after lightning often signals that a storm is close.

clue.text: Dull poet makes a comeback

indicators.note: coming back means travelling the other way, so the word for the poet is read backwards

parts.note: a bard is a poet

explanation.surface: A tedious poet returns to the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Drab describes something colourless and dreary, a close synonym of dull.

clue.text: Soldiers managed to go on skis regularly

indicators.note: to go on means to be added next, so the letters follow the word for managed

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the word that comes before

explanation.surface: Troops manage to travel on skis now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: The ranks are ordinary soldiers, as opposed to officers.

clue.text: Dead excited?

definitions.meaning: a dead body no longer breathes
someone very excited or eager may be panting for air

explanation.definitionFit: Breathless means without breath, as the dead are, and also gasping with excitement.

clue.text: Tree from Rome raised in the centre?

indicators.note: the middle letter is turned upside down, its foot raised to the top, so an M becomes a W

parts.note: something from Rome is Roman

explanation.surface: A tree brought from Rome is grown in the middle of a garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised in the centre' means turning the middle letter of ROMAN upside down: M inverted looks like W.
explanation.definitionFit: The rowan, or mountain ash, is a tree with red berries.

clue.text: Host's hair formed into a rounded mass after a twirl

indicators.note: the hair piece comes after the letter given by the clue's second 'a'

parts.words: hair formed into a rounded mass
parts.note: a bun is hair coiled into a round knot
a twirl round the floor is a dance

explanation.surface: A hostess's hair is pinned into a bun after she spins around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Host's' is the definition plus 's for 'is'; the host here is a great number, not a party-giver.
explanation.definitionFit: A host can mean a great multitude, as in a host of daffodils, which is plenty.

clue.text: Plans of French to cover up peccadillos

indicators.note: in a down answer, covering means sitting on top, so the French word goes above the next piece

parts.note: de is French for of
peccadillos are minor sins, small vices

explanation.surface: A Frenchman's schemes are designed to hide his little sins.
explanation.definitionFit: Devices are schemes or tricks, as in left to one's own devices.

clue.text: Swimming deep, lad prayed

indicators.note: swimming suggests the letters are moving about, so these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A boy out of his depth in the water prays for rescue.
explanation.definitionFit: To pray in the old sense is to beg or entreat, which is to plead.

clue.text: Six with place to stay

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
to place something is to sit it down

explanation.surface: Six people want somewhere to stay the night.
explanation.definitionFit: A visit is a stay with someone or somewhere for a short time.

clue.text: Company's salesman turning up earlier, first in store

indicators.note: in a down answer, turning up means reading upwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
former means earlier

indicators.note: first in points to the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A firm's sales rep arrives early, first into the shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Company's' is the definition plus 's for 'is'; the company here is a troupe of actors.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatrical company is a group of actors and entertainers.

clue.text: Former lover sat naked

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
a model who sat for a painter posed

explanation.surface: An old flame modelled in the nude.
explanation.definitionFit: Exposed means uncovered and laid bare, which is what naked describes.

clue.text: Boss sent to dismiss second undergraduate

parts.note: a stud or boss is a round knob on a surface

indicators.note: dismissing means sending away, so one letter is taken out of the word sent

explanation.surface: A manager is told to sack a second university student.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' looks like a manager, but it is a round raised knob, like a stud.
explanation.definitionFit: An undergraduate is a university student working towards a first degree.

clue.text: Concert — remember having no conclusion about it

indicators.note: about means going round, so the shortened word surrounds the next piece
with no ending, so the final letter of the word for remember is dropped

parts.note: to recall is to remember

explanation.surface: Someone recalls a concert but cannot recall how it ended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having no conclusion' leaves RECAL, and 'about' wraps it round the next piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A recital is a musical performance, typically by a soloist, so a kind of concert.

clue.text: Doctor Matt enters, not coming to a conclusion to give this?

definitions.text: Doctor Matt enters, not coming to a conclusion to give this?

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are rearranged
not reaching an end, so the last letter of enters is dropped

explanation.surface: Dr Matt walks in, but stops short before giving what a doctor gives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not coming to a conclusion' cuts ENTERS to ENTER; 'Doctor' rearranges MATT plus ENTER. The whole clue also describes what a doctor provides.
explanation.definitionFit: Medical treatment is what a doctor gives a patient.

clue.text: Working out four and ten — that's a large sum

indicators.note: working something out means sorting it, so these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A child adding four and ten is told the total is huge.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortune is a very large amount of money.

clue.text: Cross when captivated by pen — see high price

indicators.note: being captivated means held captive, so the letter is held inside the rearranged letters
high can mean intoxicated, so the letters are muddled

parts.note: a cross is the letter X, as in the multiplication sign

explanation.surface: Someone is annoyed at the high price of a fancy pen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high' is the anagram signal, not part of 'high price'; 'price' alone is the definition. 'when captivated by' wraps the scrambled EPENSE round X.
explanation.definitionFit: An expense is a cost, the price paid for something.

clue.text: Notices time, getting hindered by difficult questions

indicators.note: being hindered means being held in by something, so the letter sits inside the word for tough questions

parts.note: posers are puzzling questions

explanation.surface: Someone notices that time is being lost to tricky questions.
explanation.definitionFit: Posters are printed notices put up on walls.

clue.text: Power concerned with minister is imaginary

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for power in physics
re means about or concerning
to minister to someone is to tend them

explanation.surface: Power linked to a government minister is only make-believe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minister' looks like a noun, but it is a verb meaning to look after.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretend as an adjective, as in a pretend castle, means make-believe or not real.

clue.text: Fury when moving Queen's stove

indicators.note: moving tells us one letter of the word for fury is shifted to a new place

parts.note: anger is fury
R stands for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: The monarch's cooker is moved and she is furious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' takes the R of ANGER from the end to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A range is a large cooking stove, like an Aga.

clue.text: Sound emerging from soprano is exquisite

indicators.note: emerging from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A beautiful sound comes from a fine soprano.
explanation.definitionFit: A noise is any sound, though often an unwanted one.

clue.text: Check before opening

parts.note: pre- is a prefix meaning before
a vent is an opening that lets air out

explanation.surface: Someone inspects a building before it opens.
explanation.definitionFit: To check something is to stop or hold it back, which is to prevent it.

clue.text: Spear carrier starts to tire, resourcefully flipping axe around

indicators.note: around means the flipped word goes round the other letters
flipping means turning over, so the word axe is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: starts to points to the opening letters of the next two words

explanation.surface: A tired soldier with a spear cleverly twirls his axe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' makes EXA, and 'around' wraps that round the two opening letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A spear carrier is a theatrical term for an actor with a tiny non-speaking role, a walk-on.

clue.text: Indication of sadness right after meal

indicators.note: after places the letter behind the word for meal

parts.note: tea is a light afternoon or evening meal

explanation.surface: Someone is sad once a meal is over.
explanation.definitionFit: A tear rolling down the cheek is a sign that someone is unhappy.

clue.text: Is fish tailless in river? That's life

indicators.note: in means the letters go inside the river's name

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, England
taken as written

indicators.note: without its tail, so the last letter of the fish is lost

parts.note: a tench is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A philosopher asks whether a fish without a tail in a river is really alive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tailless' cuts TENCH to TENC; the Exe is a river in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Existence means being alive, so it stands for life.

clue.text: This writer following article's message

indicators.note: following puts the setter's pronoun after the article

parts.note: the definite article is a word of grammar
the setter calling themself this writer means me

explanation.surface: A columnist explains the point of their piece.
explanation.definitionFit: The theme of a work is its central idea or message.

clue.text: The woman with diamonds to take off

parts.note: she is a pronoun for a woman
D is the abbreviation for diamonds in card games

explanation.surface: A woman removes her diamond jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: To shed something is to cast it off, as a snake does its skin.

clue.text: Theresa May almost moved to embrace leader of department, one high up in education

indicators.note: embracing means holding in the arms, so the rearranged letters wrap round the next letter
moved shows the letters are shifted into a new order
almost means not quite all, so the last letter of the name is dropped
leader of points to the opening letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Former Prime Minister Theresa May was nearly persuaded to hug a senior education official.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims MAY to MA; 'moved' rearranges THERESAMA, which 'to embrace' wraps round D.
explanation.definitionFit: A head teacher is the person in charge of a school, near the top of education.
